blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights the extension of word vectors to sentences, paragraphs, and documents by Le and Mikolov, enabling distributed representations that outperform state-of-the-art methods in text classification and sentiment analysis tasks. He notes that traditional bag-of-words and bag-of-n-grams models lose semantic meaning and word order information, while paragraph vectors (PV) address these limitations by incorporating a 'memory' component (paragraph token) that captures context and topic. The blog describes two variants: PV-DM (Distributed Memory) and PV-DBOW (Distributed Bag of Words), with PV-DM performing better but their combination yielding the best results. Experimental results on sentiment analysis and paragraph classification tasks show significant improvements over prior methods, demonstrating the effectiveness of paragraph vectors in capturing semantic relationships without requiring parsing.
paper_title: Distributed Representations of Sentences and Documents
paper_abstract: Many machine learning algorithms require the input to be represented as a fixed-length feature vector. When it comes to texts, one of the most common fixed-length features is bag-of-words. Despite their popularity, bag-of-words features have two major weaknesses: they lose the ordering of the words and they also ignore semantics of the words. For example, “powerful,” “strong” and “Paris” are equally distant. In this paper, we propose Paragraph Vector, an unsupervised algorithm that learns fixed-length feature representations from variable-length pieces of texts, such as sentences, paragraphs, and documents. Our algorithm represents each document by a dense vector which is trained to predict words in the document. Its construction gives our algorithm the potential to overcome the weaknesses of bag-ofwords models. Empirical results show that Paragraph Vectors outperform bag-of-words models as well as other techniques for text representations. Finally, we achieve new state-of-the-art results on several text classification and sentiment analysis tasks.
